title.narrative: AgriGRADE Tanzania

description.narrative: AgriGRADE is a Dutch-led innovative initiative aimed at driving the sustainable inclusion of smallholder farmers in commercial supply chains. It leverages farmer organizations, agribusinesses and financial institutions to create viable, resilient, and inclusive rural economies, to tackle global challenges such as climate change, population growth, and food security.AgriGRADE addresses these challenges by providing a coordinated and integrated model to professionalize farmer organizations, optimize value chains, and link rural enterprises to finance, ultimately transforming rural economies into sustainable and inclusive systems.

In Tanzania, AgriGRADE focuses on professionalizing farmer organizations within the beans, maize and rice value chains, partnering with two local agri-SMEs, Raphael Group Limited (RGL) and Union Service Stores Limited (USSL), as primary off-takers who provide a guaranteed market for the farmers organizations as well as market incentives and business development services to stimulate the growth and professionalization of the FOs. The project focuses its activities in two intervention areas, the Northeast and the Southern Highlands of Tanzania. These two regions are conformed of: Arusha, Kilimanjaro, Manyara, and Singida regions in the Northeast of Tanzania, and Mbeya, Ruvuma, and Songwe regions in the Southern Highlands.

The long-term mission of AgriGRADE is to transform rural economies into economically viable,resilient, and inclusive systems that contribute to improved food trade, food security, and create local economic value. AgriGRADE’s vision is to modernize the agricultural sector in emerging economies and make it investable. This goes through a transformation of the way programs dedicated on professionalization of farmers organizations are done. It relies on six key principles: (1) a unified goal, (2) market driven, (3) interoperability between partners through standardized data, (4) clear division of roles defining clear responsibilities, (5) quality seal binding partners to high standards and,(6) continuous learning process.AgriGRADE focuses on strengthening farmers organizations and agri-SMEs collaborating with them to build more performing systems and achieve the following objectives:Objective 1 - gain a comprehensive understanding of the existing cooperative landscape, identify farmers organizations at different levels of professionalism, and select suitable candidates for further support.Objective 2 - identify the strengths, weaknesses, and potential of selected farmers organizations and design customized graduation strategies and business development services.Objective 3 - ensure that farmers organizations are advancing to higher levels of professionalism and performance.Objective 4 - at agri-SME level, optimize sourcing and service models, reducing costs, and strengthening value chain relationships with farmers organizations. Objective 5 - facilitate access to finance and markets for eligible farmers organizations that meet predefined criteria.
